name: AI for Learning and Hobbies
objectives: Using a free AI assistant, ask it to teach a topic step by step, saying what you know and asking it to wait for "next", getting small steps you can follow at your pace
After a short lesson, ask the assistant to quiz you one question at a time and explain again anything you miss, answering at least 2 of 3 questions in your own words
Given a hobby or topic you care about, ask for a two-week learning plan that fits your time, supplies and energy, with one small goal per day, written on your calendar or paper
Given a skill that is easier to learn by watching, search YouTube for a beginner how-to video and skip ads and sign-up links, choosing a clear beginner video

chapters.name: Chapter 1: AI as your patient tutor

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Asking AI to teach you, one step at a time
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant to teach a topic in small, clear steps at your pace.
This lesson builds toward: Using a free AI assistant, you will ask it to teach a topic step by step, saying what you know and asking it to wait for "next", getting small steps you can follow at your pace.
An AI assistant can act like a patient tutor. It will explain something as many times as you need, in as many ways as you need, and it never gets tired of questions.
Tell it what you want to learn, what you already know, and how you like to learn. For example: "I want to start bird watching in my backyard. I am a complete beginner. Teach me the first three things to know, one at a time, in short sentences. Wait for me to say 'next' before going on."
Asking it to wait for "next" keeps each step small, so you can try it or think about it before moving on.
Step by step:
- Say what you want to learn.
- Say what you already know, even if it is nothing.
- Ask for short, simple steps.
- Ask it to wait for you to say "next".
Words to know:
- Tutor: a teacher who helps one person learn at their own pace.
Try it now: Pick a topic you are curious about. Ask an assistant to teach you the first three things to know, one at a time, waiting for you to say "next". Go through all three.
You can now ask an AI assistant to teach you a topic in small steps at your own pace.

check.q: Why can an AI assistant be a good tutor?
options: It explains again as many times and ways as you need, without getting tired
It grades you like a school
check.why: The lesson says an assistant is like a patient tutor that never tires of questions.

check.q: You want to learn to play the harmonica and have never tried. What do you tell the assistant?
options: "I am a complete beginner. Teach me the first three things, one at a time. Wait for me to say next."
check.why: Saying what you know and asking for small steps that wait for "next" keeps learning at your pace.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Quizzing yourself to remember more
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant to quiz you on what you just learned.
This lesson builds toward: After a short lesson, you will ask the assistant to quiz you one question at a time and explain again anything you miss, answering at least 2 of 3 questions in your own words.
We remember more when we try to recall something, not just read it again. A short quiz is one of the best ways to make new learning stick.
After a lesson, ask: "Quiz me with three easy questions about what you just taught me. Ask one at a time and tell me if I am right." Answer in your own words. If you get one wrong, ask it to explain again in a different way.
Try the same quiz again the next day. A little practice spread over several days works better than a lot all at once.
Step by step:
- Finish a short lesson.
- Ask for three easy questions, one at a time.
- Answer in your own words.
- Ask for a new explanation of anything you missed.
- Repeat the quiz tomorrow.
Words to know:
- Recall: bringing something back to mind from memory.
Try it now: Ask the assistant to quiz you with three questions about what it taught you in Lesson 1. Answer them one at a time.
You can now use AI to quiz yourself and remember more of what you learn.

check.q: Why does a short quiz help you learn?
options: Trying to recall something helps you remember it
It gives you a grade for your records
check.why: We remember more when we try to recall something, not just read it again.

check.q: You missed one quiz question about bird calls. What do you do?
options: Ask it to explain that part again in a different way
check.why: Ask for a new explanation of anything you missed, then try again.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Making a simple learning plan
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Ask an AI assistant for a short, realistic learning plan.
This lesson builds toward: Given a hobby or topic you care about, you will ask for a two-week learning plan that fits your time, supplies and energy, with one small goal per day, written on your calendar or paper.
A plan turns "someday" into "today". Ask the assistant for a two-week plan with short sessions that fit your energy and schedule.
For example: "Make me a two-week plan to learn basic watercolor painting. I can practice 20 minutes a day, five days a week. I have a small paint set and paper. Keep each day to one small goal."
Look over the plan and change anything that does not fit. Ask it to make the days easier, shorter, or to add rest days. Then write the plan on your calendar or on paper by your chair.
Step by step:
- Say what you want to learn and for how long.
- Say how many minutes and days you can practice.
- Say what supplies you already have.
- Ask for one small goal per day.
- Adjust the plan, then write it down.
Words to know:
- Learning plan: a list of what to practice each day to reach a goal.
Try it now: Ask an assistant for a two-week learning plan for your topic, with one small goal a day and the time you can give. Make one change so it fits you better, then write down the first three days.
You can now make a realistic learning plan with AI that fits your time and energy.

check.q: What should a good learning plan have each day?
options: One small goal that fits your time
check.why: One small goal per day turns "someday" into "today".

check.q: The plan the AI gave you feels too tiring. What do you do?
options: Ask it to make the days shorter or add rest days
check.why: You can ask the assistant to change the plan so it fits your energy.

chapters.name: Chapter 2: Enjoying your hobbies with AI

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Finding good how-to videos
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Search for a helpful how-to video and judge whether it is a good one.
This lesson builds toward: Given a skill that is easier to learn by watching, you will search YouTube for a beginner how-to video and skip ads and sign-up links, choosing a clear beginner video.
Some skills are easier to learn by watching: a knitting stitch, pruning roses, a chord on the guitar. YouTube has free how-to videos on almost every hobby.
Ask an AI assistant for good search words first: "What should I search on YouTube to learn a beginner knit stitch?" Then open YouTube, tap the search box (the magnifying glass), and type those words. Look for videos made for beginners, with clear titles and helpful comments.
You can pause, go back and watch again as many times as you like. Be careful with ads and links in video descriptions that ask you to buy things or sign up; you do not need them to learn.
Step by step:
- Ask AI for good search words.
- Open YouTube and tap the magnifying glass.
- Type the words and look for beginner videos.
- Pause and replay as often as you need.
- Skip ads and links that ask you to buy or sign up.
Words to know:
- YouTube: a free website and app with videos on almost every subject.
- Search box: where you type words to find something; often shown by a magnifying glass.
Try it now: Ask an AI assistant what to search on YouTube for the first day of your learning plan. Search for it, watch one beginner video, and pause it at least once to try a step.
You can now find a helpful beginner video and learn from it at your own pace.

check.q: What does the magnifying glass on YouTube do?
check.why: The magnifying glass is the search button where you type your words.

check.q: A knitting video shows a link to "buy the full course". What do you do?
options: Skip it; you do not need it to learn
Enter your card number to see more
check.why: Ads and links that ask you to buy or sign up are not needed to learn.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Using AI for a hobby project
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use an AI assistant to plan a real hobby project from start to finish.
This lesson builds toward: Given a hobby project such as a garden or scrapbook, you will ask for a supply list and simple steps, and check safety facts with a label or trusted source, before you buy or use anything risky.
AI can help you plan a project: a small vegetable garden, a scrapbook for a grandchild's birthday, a family recipe book, or a birdhouse.
Describe the project and ask for a supply list and steps: "Help me make a small scrapbook of my granddaughter's first year. List the supplies and the steps. Keep it simple." For a garden, add your area and season: "I live in Ohio and have a sunny patio. What are three easy vegetables to grow in pots this spring?"
For anything about safety, such as tools, chemicals or plants that may be harmful to pets, check the label or a trusted source like your local garden center or library.
Step by step:
- Describe the project and who it is for.
- Add your area, season or space if it matters.
- Ask for a supply list and simple steps.
- Check safety facts with a label or trusted source.
Words to know:
- Supply list: the things you need to gather before starting a project.
Try it now: Pick a small project related to your topic. Ask an assistant for a supply list and simple steps, and circle the supplies you already have.
You can now plan a hobby project with AI, from supplies to steps.

options: A list of stores near you
A list of friends who can help
The things you need before you start a project
check.why: A supply list shows what you need before you begin.

check.q: The AI suggests a plant for your patio, and you have a cat. What do you do?
options: Ask the AI if it is sure
Check with your garden center or the plant label whether it is safe for pets
check.why: Safety facts, such as plants that may harm pets, are checked with a label or trusted source.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Exploring family history and stories
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI to help write down a family story to share.
This lesson builds toward: Given a family memory, you will write a short family story in your voice with AI help, looking up records on trusted sites instead of AI, with no private details of living relatives.
Many older adults love to explore family history and pass stories down to grandchildren. AI can help you turn memories into a short story others will enjoy.
Tell it a memory in your own words: "My father ran a bakery in 1950s Chicago. I helped on Saturdays. Help me write this as a one-page story for my grandchildren, in my voice." Then make changes so it sounds like you.
AI does not know your family's real history, so do not ask it to fill in facts about your ancestors; it may invent them. For records, websites like FamilySearch (free) or your local library's genealogy help desk are better places to look. Keep private details of living relatives out of AI.
Step by step:
- Tell AI a memory in your own words.
- Ask for a one-page story in your voice.
- Change anything that does not sound like you.
- Look up records on trusted sites, not in AI.
- Share the story with family.
Words to know:
- Genealogy: the study of family history and ancestors.
- Ancestor: a family member from long ago, such as a great-grandparent.
Try it now: Final task: choose one hobby or topic, ask an AI assistant for a two-week plan, have it teach you the first lesson step by step, let it quiz you with three questions, and write down one thing you will practice tomorrow.
You can now use AI to learn, plan hobby projects and record family stories.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Two-week plan No plan, or a plan that does not fit your time or supplies. A two-week plan with short daily sessions and one small goal each day. Adjusted the plan to add rest days or easier days, and wrote it down. First lesson step by step Asked for everything at once. Asked the assistant to teach the first lesson step by step at your pace. Said what you already know so the steps started at the right level. Quizzed yourself Skipped the quiz. Answered three quiz questions, one at a time, in your own words. Asked for a new explanation of anything missed and tried again. Next practice Nothing written for tomorrow. Wrote down one thing to practice tomorrow. Chose a time for it and put it on your calendar. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.why: Genealogy is the study of family history.

check.q: You want to know where your great-grandmother was born. Where do you look?
options: Ask the AI to fill it in
Guess and write it in the story
FamilySearch or your library's genealogy help desk
check.why: AI may invent family facts; real records are on trusted sites or at the library.
